cover_options.text: Anthropic launches Claude as a sidebar inside Google Docs, Sheets and Slides
Claude can now edit your Google Docs, Sheets and Slides. Anthropic says it asks first.
Anthropic takes Claude into Google's office apps, where Google's Gemini already lives

headline.text: Claude gets a sidebar in Google Docs, Sheets and Slides

body.text: On October 6, 2026, Anthropic put Claude for Google Workspace into public beta on all paid Claude plans. One install from the Google Workspace Marketplace covers all three apps.

headline.text: Gemini is already built in here

body.text: 9to5Google notes that Gemini can already be used natively in Google Workspace apps, and frames the Claude add-on as useful for people already invested in Claude.

headline.text: It reads the file and edits it directly

body.text: Anthropic says Claude opens beside the file, sees selected text, cells or slides, and edits directly. In Sheets it can build pivot tables and charts; in Slides it flags overlapping or off-slide elements.

headline.text: A second door opens from Claude chat

body.text: Anthropic says new Docs, Sheets and Slides connectors, also in beta, let Claude create and edit Google files from the chat. On Team and Enterprise plans, an owner must enable them first.

headline.text: By default, edits wait for your approval

body.text: Anthropic says each change appears as an approval card by default, while an accept-all mode applies edits without stopping. Some actions, such as adding a link, always pause.

headline.text: Files from outsiders can carry hidden instructions

body.text: Prompt injection is hidden instructions in a file, such as white text, that try to steer an AI. Anthropic says users should still review proposed actions, especially in files from outside their organization.

slides.quote_excerpt: Claude treats document content as data rather than commands, labels hidden text it finds

headline.text: Google halts any single operation at this mark

body.text: Long tasks can stop partway. Anthropic also lists no Firefox support, no comment access in Docs, and Slides charts that don't update.
The capability, privacy and security claims all come from Anthropic. The sources found no independent hands-on testing, no Google reaction and no end date for the beta.

caption.text:
Anthropic put Claude for Google Workspace into public beta on October 6, 2026, adding a Claude sidebar to Google Docs, Sheets and Slides on all paid Claude plans. Anthropic says it also released beta connectors that let Claude create and edit Google files from the Claude chat. (Public beta means a release open to all eligible users that Anthropic says still has known limits.)

Claude can edit files directly. Anthropic says it asks for approval before changes by default and always pauses before adding a link or removing anyone's access. Its beta limits include no Firefox support and Google's six-minute cap on any single operation. Gemini is already built into these Google apps, and 9to5Google frames the add-on as useful for people already invested in Claude. The capability and security claims come from Anthropic, and the sources found no independent testing.

Would you let an AI edit your shared documents without asking first?

edit_notes: Cover leads with Anthropic (well_known true) and what it did; launch is independently reported, so no 'says' on the cover, but capability claims on slides keep 'Anthropic says'.
Slide 3 is the one background slide (Gemini already native, B1/F11), attributed to 9to5Google.
Quote slide uses an exact excerpt of Q2 (88 chars) to stay under 140; the prompt injection gloss comes from TERMS.
The 'review proposed actions, especially in outside files' line comes from the brief's why_it_matters (F5, F6, F9) and is attributed to Anthropic.
Did not use N2 (30 days): single-source via Unite.AI and not confirmed in the Help Center.
Did not use F8, F10 or F13 (plans, permissions, enterprise features) to keep the story tight; they are secondary to the launch.

Slides 2, 3, 5, 6 and the landing have image none: the content is about software behavior and ideas, and no physical thing is mentioned. Anthropic's logo is used only on the cover and the quote slide.
Slide 4 uses a stock spreadsheet scene because the slide mentions cells and Sheets.
Stat slide uses N1 with a headline that explains it without repeating the figure; Firefox, comments and charts limits attributed to Anthropic's list (F9).
Landing slide states the NOT ANSWERED gaps (no independent testing, no Google reaction, no beta end date) without inventing suspense.
Caption's Gemini and six-minute clauses reuse slide content; no new facts added.
